speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your follow-up. You mentioned occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain occurring while eating suggests referred otalgia, possibly from the auriculotemporal nerve; is the pain sharp and radiating to your jaw or temple? Also, when you wear earrings, is the discomfort localized to the piercing site or a deeper sensation within the ear canal?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (with possible granulation tissue or residual cholesteatoma in the right ear).

The shooting pain triggered by chewing (jaw movement) is classic for auriculotemporal neuralgia, likely due to nerve irritation post-surgery. The discomfort with earrings suggests residual granulation tissue or a small cholesteatoma causing canal expansion, which I suspect based on your history of recurrent ear infections and the poor sleep/stress factors that can heighten pain perception. While I have requested an otoscopy to visualize the canal, the clinical picture of post-tympanoplasty shooting pain with mastication strongly points to this neuralgia.
